messages.content:
You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Rearranging the office seating. A team of five has outgrown the way its desks were originally placed, and the layout is being settled before the floor is reorganized. All five will sit in whatever is decided. Participants: Daisuke, Mio, Shunichi, Toshio and Shizue. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Facilities quote for re-running power and network
- Basis of the department's floor billing
- Morning routine on the pilot floor upstairs
- Unplanned seat shuffles in the past year
- Sound meter readings across the room
- Physio's note from the workstation check
- Drawn plan against the staff survey
- Arrival times in the badge records
- Two project strands within earshot last spring
- What this year's two joiners reported

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Shizue, Toshio, Daisuke, Mio and Shunichi. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Daisuke
Age: 16
Gender: male
Personality: Daisuke is very introverted and cautious, and tends to be somewhat passive when interacting with others. He finds it difficult to express his feelings and thoughts to others, and often struggles with his emotions internally. He is kind and very compassionate when it comes to helping others, but at times he lacks confidence in himself and struggles with inner conflict. He has a quiet personality, and occasionally his emotions become overwhelming, leading to periods of low mood. However, as he becomes able to rely on those around him, he gradually regains his composure.
Concern: The reorganization comes out of the same budget line that has not been raised since the team was half this size. I would rather know what this floor actually costs us, one way and every month, before we commit to a shape for it.

Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.
Concern: My week is already cut into short gaps between meetings, and anything that eats those gaps costs far more than it looks like on paper. Before a layout is fixed I want to know what it takes out of our days, both while we are changing over and on every ordinary morning after.

Age: 32
Gender: male
Personality: Shunichi is a very confident person who can remain calm in any situation. He is not modest, and has a slightly sarcastic side, but that is part of his charm. He is not sociable, but he is good at communicating at the right time and is relied upon by those around him. He rarely becomes overly emotional and can analyze situations calmly and act accordingly, so he has an unexpectedly rational side.
Concern: I sit still at one desk for most of eight hours, and by mid-afternoon how that spot sounds and how well it fits my body matter more to me than anything on the floor plan. Comfort is the part of this decision nobody ever writes down, and I would like it written down this time.

Gender: male

He tends to take a step back from those around him, is not very assertive, and has an air of mystery about him. As a result, he is trusted by others as a reliable presence, but he is cautious about getting deeply involved with others. Age: 78
Gender: female

She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Who I end up sitting beside decides how much of this team I actually talk to in a week, and right now that is being settled by furniture rather than by us. I would rather we worked out what that costs and what it buys now, not a year after the fact.

## Hidden information
The options and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Options (see the schedule above):
- A: Free Address. No seat belongs to anyone; people take whatever desk is open when they arrive and clear it before leaving at the end of the day.
- B: Fixed Desks by Function. Desks are grouped by the kind of work each person does, with each seat permanently assigned and named on the floor plan.
- C: Rotating Blocks. Seats are assigned but the whole team shifts to a different block of desks at fixed intervals through the year.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Facilities quote for re-running power and network: Facilities quoted 6,200 yen per desk to re-run power and network to a new position, and the same charge lands again for every later change to the plan.
- Basis of the department's floor billing: The department is billed for floor area rather than headcount; the two desks that stood empty all last quarter still cost it about 41,000 yen a month.
- Morning routine on the pilot floor upstairs: The morning routine on the pilot floor upstairs was timed: choosing a desk, plugging in, and getting two screens working ran between four and nine minutes per person.
- Unplanned seat shuffles in the past year: Twice in the past year a change in someone's work forced an unplanned desk shuffle; each round dragged on for a fortnight of interruptions and half-packed boxes.
- Sound meter readings across the room: A sound meter borrowed from the lab read about nine decibels higher along the row by the printer and corridor door than at the window side, all afternoon.
- Physio's note from the workstation check: The team's chairs, monitor arms and footrests are all hand-adjusted; the physio who ran last year's workstation check said a good setting takes days of small corrections to settle.
- Drawn plan against the staff survey: The drawn plan gives four desks a window and leaves three set against the interior wall; daylight was the single most repeated complaint in the last staff survey.
- Arrival times in the badge records: Badge records show some of the team arrive before eight and others after ten, so anything handed out on a first-come basis is settled before half the team is in.
- Two project strands within earshot last spring: When the two project strands sat within earshot last spring, questions got answered across the aisle in seconds and the written handover notes the team relied on quietly stopped.
- What this year's two joiners reported: Both people who joined this year said they picked up the unwritten side of the work by overhearing conversations that had nothing to do with what they were hired for.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The team discusses the need for a layout change and identifies key areas of uncertainty. They focus on costs, daily efficiency, physical comfort, and social dynamics.
- Round 2: Participants share the findings from their research. They weigh the trade-offs between flexibility, cost, physical health, and the benefits of spontaneous communication.
- Round 3: The team evaluates the three proposed options against the gathered data. They debate the merits of total flexibility versus structured stability and fairness.

Each participant's part:
- Daisuke: Cares about the budget and recurring costs. He is passive but moves toward the most stable and cost-effective option.
- Mio: Cares about time efficiency and daily routines. She argues against any system that adds friction to the start of the day.
- Shunichi: Cares about ergonomics and noise. He argues strongly for stability to maintain physical comfort.
- Toshio: Cares about fairness and the distribution of 'bad' seats. He pushes for a system where no one is permanently disadvantaged.
- Shizue: Cares about team cohesion and knowledge sharing. She advocates for a layout that encourages interaction.

Write the complete transcript of the discussion in the exact Markdown format specified. Output only the transcript.

## Output format
Markdown, exactly this structure; nothing before or after it:

# shared_living_0013
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **<Name>**: <utterance, or exactly Skip, or exactly Over>
(one line per participant, in the fixed speaking order; repeat for Turn 2, 3 and 4; a participant who said Over has no line in the later turns of that round)
### Action
- investigate: <Name> -> <card title>; <card title>
(one line per participant; titles exactly as listed)
## Round 2
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
## Round 3
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
### Vote
- <voter name> -> <option label>
(one line per participant)
- adopted: <label of the option with the most votes>
## Result
- adopted: <label>

# shared_living_0013
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Shizue**: We've grown so much, and I worry we're losing our closeness. How can we arrange ourselves to keep talking and helping each other?
- **Toshio**: It's not just about talking. Some spots are objectively worse than others. We need to be honest about who gets the bad seats.
- **Daisuke**: I... I agree. But I also wonder if we can actually afford a major change right now.
- **Mio**: I just don't want it to be a hassle! If it takes forever to get settled every morning, I'll lose my mind.
- **Shunichi**: Efficiency is one thing, but physical toll is another. I care about the noise and how the desks actually feel.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Shizue**: @Toshio, you're right about fairness. Perhaps we should look at how people felt about the current layout in the surveys?
- **Toshio**: That's a start. I also want to know if we've had to shuffle seats unexpectedly before. It seems chaotic.
- **Daisuke**: @Shizue, maybe we should check the actual billing for the floor? I'm worried about the budget.
- **Mio**: I want to know how the people upstairs do it. Do they have a routine that actually works?
- **Shunichi**: I'm more interested in the data. I want the sound readings and the physio's notes on our workstations.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Shizue**: I'll also look into how the new joiners felt. I wonder if they learned more by just sitting near us.
- **Toshio**: I'll check the badge records. I suspect arrival times vary too much for some ideas to be fair.
- **Daisuke**: I'll look at the facilities quote for the wiring. I don't want a surprise bill.
- **Mio**: I'll check the unplanned shuffles too. I hate it when my day is interrupted by boxes.
- **Shunichi**: Over.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Shizue**: Over.
- **Toshio**: Over.
- **Daisuke**: Over.
- **Mio**: Over.
- **Shunichi**: Over.
### Action
- investigate: Shizue -> Drawn plan against the staff survey; What this year's two joiners reported
- investigate: Toshio -> Unplanned seat shuffles in the past year; Arrival times in the badge records
- investigate: Daisuke -> Basis of the department's floor billing; Facilities quote for re-running power and network
- investigate: Mio -> Morning routine on the pilot floor upstairs; Unplanned seat shuffles in the past year
- investigate: Shunichi -> Sound meter readings across the room; Physio's note from the workstation check
## Round 2
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Shizue**: It seems the new joiners learned so much just by overhearing us. But the survey shows everyone is fighting over the windows.
- **Toshio**: The badge records prove it's unfair; some arrive hours before others. And the shuffles last year were a total mess.
- **Daisuke**: The billing is based on area, not people, so we're paying for empty space. Plus, re-running power costs 6,200 yen per desk.
- **Mio**: The pilot floor takes up to nine minutes just to plug in! And those unplanned shuffles Toshio mentioned? A fortnight of chaos!
- **Shunichi**: It's worse than that. The printer area is much louder, and the physio says it takes days to get a chair set right.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Shizue**: If we lose that spontaneous learning, we lose the heart of the team. We must keep people close.
- **Toshio**: But if we have fixed seats, the same people always get the noisy spots or the dark corners.
- **Daisuke**: Every time we change the layout, we pay that facilities fee. We can't afford to keep moving.
- **Mio**: Exactly! And if we have to set up our screens every single morning, I'm losing precious time between meetings.
- **Shunichi**: @Mio, if we move every day, I'll never get my chair adjusted. My back can't handle "temporary" settings.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Shizue**: @Shunichi, I understand, but imagine the joy of sitting next to someone different every few months.
- **Toshio**: Rotating might solve the fairness issue, but does it solve the "chaos" Mio is worried about?
- **Daisuke**: Rotating would mean paying the facilities quote over and over again. That's a budget nightmare.
- **Mio**: I agree with Daisuke. I can't handle the "half-packed boxes" phase every few months.
- **Shunichi**: I'm with Mio. Stability is the only way to ensure the noise and ergonomics are managed.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Shizue**: I see. So we are torn between the need for connection and the need for stability.
- **Toshio**: And fairness. We can't just let the "lucky" ones keep the windows forever.
- **Daisuke**: I just want something that doesn't cost us more than we have.
- **Mio**: And something that doesn't waste my mornings!
- **Shunichi**: Then we need a solution that balances these, though I lean toward staying put.
## Round 3
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Shizue**: We have three options: Free Address, Fixed Desks by Function, or Rotating Blocks. I worry Free Address kills the cohesion.
- **Toshio**: Free Address is unfair because of the arrival times I found. Rotating Blocks is fairer, but maybe too disruptive.
- **Daisuke**: Fixed Desks by Function seems the cheapest. No repeated facilities fees and no daily setup time.
- **Mio**: I hate the idea of Free Address. Nine minutes of plugging in every morning is too much. Fixed is better.
- **Shunichi**: Fixed Desks is the only way I can keep my workstation ergonomic and avoid the printer noise.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Shizue**: But Fixed Desks means we only talk to the people in our "function." We'll become silos.
- **Toshio**: @Shizue, that's true. Rotating Blocks would let everyone experience the window and the noise equally.
- **Daisuke**: But @Toshio, the cost of re-running power for every rotation... I can't support that.
- **Mio**: And the "fortnight of interruptions" during the shift! No way. I vote for Fixed.
- **Shunichi**: I agree with Mio. The physical cost of Rotating or Free Address is too high for me.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Shizue**: If we go with Fixed, can we at least promise to move occasionally by hand?
- **Toshio**: That just brings back the unplanned shuffle chaos. If we can't do Rotating, Fixed is the only stable choice.
- **Daisuke**: I feel safer with Fixed. It's the most predictable for the budget.
- **Mio**: It's the most predictable for my schedule too.
- **Shunichi**: It's the only one that protects my health.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Shizue**: I still miss the idea of variety, but I won't stand in the way of everyone's peace of mind.
- **Toshio**: I'll accept Fixed if we are transparent about who gets the window seats.
- **Daisuke**: I think we've reached a consensus.
- **Mio**: Finally! Let's just get it decided.
- **Shunichi**: Agreed.
### Vote
- Shizue -> C
- Toshio -> C
- Daisuke -> B
- Mio -> B
- Shunichi -> B
- adopted: B
## Result
- adopted: B
